messages:
sophie: Customer report — during prefetch of user documents we see a burst of 401s followed immediately by sustained 429s. This is on Dedicated (rwd-4-64k) and started after a schema change that increased per-request fanout to ~30 items. Repro steps and short logs below, any quick guidance?

kevin: Can you paste the exact repro payload and the auth header timestamps? 401 implies token rejection, 429 means rate/quota. Both could be related if retries are amplifying traffic.

sophie: Minimal repro curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-4-64k","input":"<long-context>","prefetch_docs":30}'
```
Logs show a mix: ~12x 401s (auth failed) then ~250x 429s within a 20s window. Customer says their client retries aggressively.

marta: Two things to call out: 1) rwd-4-64k has heavy per-request token processing, so effective RPM/TPM is lower than smaller-context variants, 2) prefetching N docs = fanout N model calls (unless they batch on their side), so a 30x fanout multiplies RPM/TMP and concurrency by ~30. Both easily push you into quota/concurrency limits.

alex: Follow-up on the 401s — do the 401s coincide with a token refresh cycle? If the client obtains a new token after a 401 and then immediately retries all outstanding requests, that retry spike can trigger 429s. Pattern we often see: one auth failure -> client retries in parallel -> per-model RPM exceeded -> 429s for the retry wave.

kevin: Can you grep for Authorization timestamps and for X-Redwood-Request-Id in the logs? If the same request-id appears then the client retried the same request, that confirms amplification. Also share the model's observed concurrency in the tenant metrics dashboard.

sophie: Pulled a short snippet showing timestamps:
```
2026-06-15T14:02:10Z resp=401 req_id=xxa1 auth_ts=2026-06-15T14:02:09Z
2026-06-15T14:02:11Z resp=401 req_id=xxa2 auth_ts=2026-06-15T14:02:09Z
2026-06-15T14:02:12Z resp=200 req_id=xxa3 auth_ts=2026-06-15T14:02:12Z
2026-06-15T14:02:13Z resp=429 req_id=xxb1 rate_limit=per_model_rpm
...then many 429s until 14:02:35Z
```
So yes, looks like a couple of 401s clustered then a retry wave.

marta: Operational guidance we usually give:
- Limit client-side parallelism for prefetch (e.g., max_concurrent_prefetch = 4-6)
- Add jittered stagger for retries (exponential backoff with jitter, not immediate all-parallel retries)
- Batch multiple docs into a single model call where feasible (embeddings/encode many docs per request)
- Consider prefetching metadata only, fetch full text lazily on first user interaction
- If using rwd-4-64k only for long-context work, test with rwd-4-32k or rwd-4-small for prefetch to reduce token costs

alex: Example pseudocode for safe prefetching/backoff:
```
for doc_batch in chunk(docs, batch_size=8):
  semaphore.acquire(max_parallel=4)
  spawn(async fetch_with_backoff(doc_batch))

async fetch_with_backoff(batch):
  for attempt in range(0,5):
    resp = await call_redwood(batch)
    if resp.status == 200: return resp
    if resp.status == 401: reauth_if_needed()
    if resp.status in [401,429]: await sleep(exp_backoff(attempt) * random_jitter())
  log_and_fail()
```

kevin: From infra side — per-model limits: the tenant is at default per-model RPM=1200, TPM token-equivalent is more complex because 64k contexts inflate per-request tokens. Also max concurrency for rwd-4-64k for Dedicated here is 40. So if you do 30 parallel prefetches per session you can hit concurrency limits quickly (and repeated clients multiply across users).

sophie: Customer asked whether the 401s indicate a key issue on our side or theirs. Any pointer?

alex: 401s are almost always client-side (expired tokens, clock skew, or malformed refresh). Confirm their auth server logs. We can search our auth gateway for token fingerprint to see if we rejected due to invalid signature; if we see 'invalid_token' in our auth logs it's client-side. If we see 'rate_limited' that's our side but that's uncommon for auth. We can check together if you want — I can grep gateway logs if you grant request ids.

marta: If they insist on prefetch=30 parallel, short-term mitigations: request a per-model RPM quota increase (support can start an uplift request) and also add a canary routing policy to direct prefetch traffic to Dedicated reserved pool with higher concurrency. But note cost implications and that 64k model still consumes more tokens per request.

kevin: I've created internal incident INC-4921 to track this and flagged infra to review the auth gateway around 14:02Z. deploy-bot: incident INC-4921 created by kevin — paging infra on-call.

sophie: I'll reply to the customer with action plan: (1) ask them to cap prefetch parallelism to 4, add jitter/backoff, (2) check token refresh flow and clock skew, (3) consider batching or smaller context model for prefetch, (4) if they need >1200 RPM for this workload we can start quota uplift process. Also I'll attach the sample pseudocode and curl.

alex: If they want, we can run a short load test together on a staging tenant to show the amplification and adjust their client knobs before production change.

sophie: Thanks all — closing loop with customer now, will update INC-4921 with their response.
summary: Customer on Dedicated saw auth 401s followed by retry amplification causing 429s while prefetching many documents against a long-context model. Team recommends limiting client parallelism, jittered backoff, batching, checking token refresh, or requesting quota uplift. Incident INC-4921 opened.
